bottom_line: Apixaban versus warfarin reduced stroke or systemic embolism (hazard ratio with apixaban, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.95).
implications: Based on the reported hazard ratios and event rates, apixaban compared with warfarin was associated with lower rates of stroke or systemic embolism (1.27% per year vs 1.60% per year; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.95), major bleeding (2.13% per year vs 3.09% per year; HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.60 to 0.80), and death from any cause (3.52% per year vs 3.94% per year; HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.80 to 0.99). The document also reports no significant difference for ischemic or uncertain type of stroke (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.13; P = 0.42).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind trial comparing apixaban 5 mg twice daily vs warfarin (INR 2.0–3.0) in 18,201 patients with atrial fibrillation and ≥1 additional stroke risk factor.
major_points.quote: In this randomized, double-blind trial, we compared apixaban (at a dose of 5 mg twice daily) with warfarin (target international normalized ratio, 2.0 to 3.0) in 18,201 patients with atrial fibrillation and at least one additional risk factor for stroke.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke or systemic embolism; trial designed for noninferiority with hierarchical testing for superiority, major bleeding, then all-cause death.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke or systemic em- bolism. The trial was designed to test for noninferiority, with key secondary objec- tives of testing for superiority with respect to the primary outcome and to the rates of major bleeding and death from any cause.

major_points.text: Primary outcome rate was 1.27%/yr with apixaban vs 1.60%/yr with warfarin (HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.66–0.95; superiority P=0.01).
major_points.quote: The rate of the primary outcome was 1.27% per year in the apixaban group, as compared with 1.60% per year in the war- farin group (hazard ratio with apixaban, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 0.95; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.01 for superiority).

major_points.text: Major bleeding was lower with apixaban (2.13%/yr) vs warfarin (3.09%/yr) (HR 0.69; 95% CI 0.60–0.80).
major_points.quote: The rate of major bleeding was 2.13% per year in the apixaban group, as compared with 3.09% per year in the war- farin group (hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.60 to 0.80; P<0.001)

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was 3.52%/yr with apixaban vs 3.94%/yr with warfarin (HR 0.89; 95% CI 0.80–0.99).
major_points.quote: the rates of death from any cause were 3.52% and 3.94%, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.80 to 0.99; P = 0.047).

absolute_effects.text: For every 1000 patients treated for 1.8 years, apixaban vs warfarin prevented stroke in 6, major bleeding in 15, and death in 8 patients.
absolute_effects.quote: For every 1000 patients treated for 1.8 years, apixaban, as compared with warfarin, prevented a stroke in 6 patients, major bleeding in 15 patients, and death in 8 patients.

subgroups.text: Primary outcome reduction was consistent across major prespecified subgroups; interaction tests not significant (P>0.10) for all 21 predefined subgroups.
subgroups.quote: The reduction in the primary outcome with apix- aban was consistent across all major subgroups (Fig. 2), and statistical tests for interaction were not significant (P>0.10) for all of the 21 pre- defined subgroups.

harms.text: Serious adverse events occurred in 35.0% with apixaban and 36.5% with warfarin.
harms.quote: serious adverse events (35.0% and 36.5% in the two groups, respectively)

harms.text: Adverse events occurred in 81.5% with apixaban and 83.1% with warfarin.
harms.quote: Adverse events occurred in almost equal propor- tions of patients in the apixaban group and in the warfarin group (81.5% of the patients in the apixaban group and 83.1% of patients in the war- farin group)

inclusion_criteria.text: Atrial fibrillation or flutter at enrollment or ≥2 episodes documented by ECG at least 2 weeks apart in prior 12 months.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligible patients had atrial fibrillation or flutter at enrollment or two or more episodes of atrial fi- brillation or flutter, as documented by electrocar- diography, at least 2 weeks apart in the 12 months before enrollment.

inclusion_criteria.text: At least one stroke risk factor required (e.g., age ≥75 years; prior stroke/TIA/systemic embolism; recent symptomatic heart failure or LVEF ≤40%; diabetes; or hypertension requiring drugs).
inclusion_criteria.quote: In addition, at least one of the following risk factors for stroke was required: an age of at least 75 years; previous stroke, transient ischemic attack, or systemic embolism; symptom- atic heart failure within the previous 3 months or left ventricular ejection fraction of no more than 40%; diabetes mellitus; or hypertension requiring pharmacologic treatment.

exclusion_criteria.text: Atrial fibrillation due to a reversible cause.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Key exclusion criteria were atrial fibrillation due to a reversible cause,
Key exclusion criteria were atrial fibrillation due to a reversible cause, moderate or severe mitral stenosis,

exclusion_criteria.text: Conditions other than atrial fibrillation that required anticoagulation (e.g., a prosthetic heart valve).
exclusion_criteria.quote: conditions other than atrial fibrillation that required anti- coagulation (e.g., a prosthetic heart valve),

exclusion_criteria.text: Need for aspirin >165 mg/day or for both aspirin and clopidogrel.
exclusion_criteria.quote: a need for aspirin at a dose of >165 mg a day or for both aspirin and clopidogrel,

analysis_methods.text: Primary and key secondary analyses used Cox proportional-hazards model with stratification factors.
analysis_methods.quote: The primary and key secondary analyses were performed with the use of the Cox proportional- hazards model, with previous warfarin status and geographic region

analysis_methods.text: Bleeding analyses included patients who received at least one dose and events through 2 days after last dose.
analysis_methods.quote: The analyses of bleeding events included all patients who re- ceived at least one dose of a study drug and in- cluded all events from the time the first dose of a study drug was received until 2 days after the last dose was received.

analysis_methods.text: Planned 90% power based on 448 primary outcome events and upper CI boundaries for relative risk.
analysis_methods.quote: we estimated that with the occurrence of the primary outcome in 448 patients, the study would have 90% power to ensure that the upper boundary of the 99% confidence interval for the relative risk would be less than 1.44

analysis_methods.text: Prespecified hierarchical sequential testing used to control overall type I error.
analysis_methods.quote: To control the overall type I error, pre- specified hierarchical sequential testing was per- formed first on the primary outcome for nonin- feriority, then on the primary outcome for superiority, then on major bleeding, and finally on death from any cause.

trial_conduct.text: Ethics committee approval obtained at all sites.
trial_conduct.quote: Approval by the appropriate ethics committees was obtained at all sites.

trial_conduct.text: Written informed consent obtained from all patients.
trial_conduct.quote: All patients provided written informed consent.

trial_conduct.text: Outcomes were adjudicated by a blinded clinical-events committee using prespecified criteria.
trial_conduct.quote: The primary and secondary efficacy and safety outcomes were adjudicated on the basis of pre- specified criteria by a clinical-events committee whose members were not aware of study-group assignments.

trial_conduct.text: Independent data and safety monitoring committee reviewed accumulating data with one prespecified interim analysis for efficacy.
trial_conduct.quote: An inde- pendent data and safety monitoring committee reviewed the accumulating trial data, with one prespecified interim analysis for efficacy.
